sources.title: Registered medical product directory (Drug Directory)
sources.publication: EDE online register at services.ede.gov.ae/drugdirectory (embedded at www.ede.gov.ae/en/drug-directory)
sources.note: Searched 25 Sep 2026 by ingredient (IngredientName, substring match) and product name (SearchTerm), e.g. https://services.ede.gov.ae/drugdirectory?IngredientName=semaglutide&ViewMode=list&PageSize=100. Every row returned was 'Active'; the directory has no status filter, so withdrawn or cancelled registrations may not appear. Rows give classification, strength, form, manufacturer, status and registration date; detail pages add dispensing mode and a therapeutic category but no indications. Quotes join table cells with ' | ' and page fields with spaces; '…' marks omitted cells or fields. Searches with no hits: retatrutide, afamelanotide, Scenesse, melanotan, Melanotan, tesamorelin, Tesamorelin, Egrifta, sermorelin, Sermorelin, ipamorelin, Ipamorelin, CJC, CJC-1295, ibutamoren, Ibutamoren, MK-677, BPC-157, BPC 157, pentadecapeptide, TB-500, TB500, thymosin, Thymosin, thymosin beta, KPV, LL-37, cathelicidin, GHK (ingredient and product name), prezatide, copper tripeptide, copper peptide, thymulin, Thymulin, PTD, DBM, PTD-DBM, Zepbound, Loniten, Minoxidil tablet, growth hormone, Skytrofa. 'BPC' as an ingredient matched only two unrelated products whose ingredients carry the 'BPC' pharmacopoeia suffix (Permethrin BPC, Cajuput Oil BPC). 'tripeptide' as an ingredient returned 7 rows: Martiderm anti-hair-loss ampoules, lotion and shampoos (biotinoyl tripeptide-1; GSL products) and the ST500 gel medical device (SH-tripeptide-1).

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE; 'UAE Drug Corporation' in the official English translation) has been the federal authority regulating medical products since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (issued 25 Sep 2023, in force 30 Sep 2023), with the power to approve and register medical products.
frameworks.quote: The Corporation shall be the federal authority responsible for regulating medical products in the State. To this end, the corporation shall be entitled to the following: … 7. Approve and register medical products and supervise them in accordance with the relevant legislations;

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the EDE succeeded the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) in regulating medical products, and the 2023 law let the Cabinet keep MOHAP exercising these powers until the EDE carried out all its operations (Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, Arts. 15-16).
frameworks.quote: The Corporation shall succeed the Ministry of Health and Prevention and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment in all rights, obligations, and legal matters pertaining to the regulation and management of medical products. … the Cabinet may assign the Ministry of Health and Prevention and the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment or any other entity to exercise the competences stipulated herein until the Corporation carries out all its operations.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, since 2 January 2025 (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, which replaced Federal Law 8/2019), no medical product may be imported, distributed, possessed, sold, displayed, used or manufactured for circulation without an EDE marketing approval.
frameworks.quote: Without prejudice to the applicable legislation concerning veterinary preparations, it is not permitted to import, distribute, possess, sell, display, re-market, use, or manufacture any Medical Product in the State for circulation therein, except after obtaining Marketing Approval of any type from the EDE.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, physicians may prescribe a medicine for uses not in its leaflet, or a medicine never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, when no equivalent alternative is available and with the patient's approval; compassionate use is excluded from this rule (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 42(1)).
frameworks.quote: Physicians may not prescribe a Medical Product for new uses not specified in the internal leaflet or electronic leaflet, or prescribe a Medical Product that has not been submitted for Marketing Approval, except when necessary, provided that there is no equivalent alternative available and with the patient approval. The compassionate use of the Medical Product is excluded from the provisions of this Clause.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, only pharmaceutical establishments may import, market, sell, display or store prescription-only medicines (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 40).
frameworks.quote: Non-Pharmaceutical Establishments are prohibited from importing, marketing, selling, displaying, storing or circulation any Medical Product that requires a prescription for dispensing.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, the DHA prohibits circulating, prescribing, dispensing, administering or using any peptide product unless it is registered or licensed with the EDE and used within the scope of its licence, and requires registered peptide products to be used strictly within their approved indications (External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: 1. It is prohibited to circulate, prescribe, dispense, administer, or use any peptide product unless it is duly registered or licensed with the Emirates Drug Establishment, and authorized for use within the scope of its license. … 3. Strict adherence to the approved indications for use of each registered or authorized product is required.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, medical products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from the marketing-approval requirement (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 5(2), in force 2 Jan 2025).
frameworks.quote: As an exception to Clause (1) of this Article, all categories of Medical Products that are compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies are exempt from the requirement to obtain Marketing Approval.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, a compounding pharmacy may not compound essential copies of products holding an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient, and may not formulate products intended for research, development or experimentation (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 95).
frameworks.quote: The Compound Pharmacy is prohibited from the following: … 4. Commencing the installation of Medical Products that are essentially copies of Medical Products that have a valid Marketing Approval from the EDE, unless there is no commercially available Medical Product that can achieve the expected direct benefit to the patient health, and similar results could not be obtained by other means. 5. Compounding Pharmacies may not conduct any activities related to improvised, unstudied formulations or the extraction process of medicines and preparations derived from natural sources, and it is not permitted to formulate a Medical Product prepared for research, development or experimentation.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH Standard for Provision of Compounding Pharmacy Services (August 2026) allows compounding only for a genuine, documented clinical need that no suitable licensed product meets, and bars copying commercially available products for convenience or cost or introducing experimental or unverified products.
frameworks.quote: Compounding shall be performed only to meet a genuine, documented clinical need where a suitable licensed commercial product does not meet the patient’s needs (e.g., required strength, dosage form, excipient restrictions, or verified shortage). Compounding shall not be used to copy or replicate commercially available products for convenience or cost, to manufacture at scale for general supply, or to introduce experimental or unverified products into the market under a pharmacy license.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, compounding requires a Good Compounding Practice (GCP) certificate issued by the EDE, and compounding from unapproved or unknown-source substances, or from substances not on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances, is prohibited unless the DoH permits it (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).
frameworks.quote: A valid Good Compounding Practice (GCP) certificate is mandatory to obtain a compounding-pharmacy service. (Local requirement: DoH/EDE) Facilities shall apply for and maintain the GCP certificate with EDE. … Experimental or unverified compounding, the use of unapproved or unknown-source substances, investigational drugs (except where supplied and used under a DoH-approved clinical trial), and any product containing banned or EDE, MOHAP, DoH-restricted substances are prohibited. Substances that are not listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (as permitted and/or under regulatory evaluation) shall not be used for routine compounding unless explicitly permitted by the DoH.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH treats peptides as emerging, non-monographed, high-risk substances: novel substances of unknown risk may be compounded only if monographed, a component of an approved medicine, or listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).
frameworks.quote: A substance defined by risk signature rather than chemical name (e.g., peptides): no monograph, marketed ahead of approval, thin evidence, identity or purity risk, or demand-driven uptake. Treated as high-risk and non-default. … Novel substances of unknown risk are considered experimental and prohibited unless the substance is monographed, is an approved medicinal product component, or is listed on the DoH Registry for Compounded Substances following regulatory review.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, where emerging substances such as peptides are permitted, prescribing is limited to eligible facilities and credentialed prescribers for accepted indications, office-stock ordering to hospitals and DoH-approved specialty clinics, and compounding pharmacies must dispense only against individual prescriptions (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).
frameworks.quote: Where permitted, prescribing and administration shall be restricted to eligible facilities and appropriately credentialed prescribers in approved specialties, commensurate with the product’s risk classification, and limited to accepted indications and eligible populations … Bulk (office-stock) ordering is restricted to hospitals and DoH-approved specialty clinics; patient-specific compounding pharmacies shall dispense only against an individual prescription and shall not supply office stock.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, compounded peptide formulations may use only certified active ingredients imported under EDE oversight, clinics must hold technical agreements with licensed compounding pharmacies, and peptide products must be traceable from source to patient (DoH Circular 148/2026, 31 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: 2. Clinics shall establish technical agreements with licensed compounding pharmacies to ensure traceability across the supply chain; 3. Only certified active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) imported under EDE oversight shall be used in compounded peptide formulations, subject to DoH verification; 4. Full traceability of peptide products from source to patient shall be maintained to ensure patient safety and regulatory compliance;

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, the DHA prohibits using any peptide product intended for research use on humans or for therapeutic purposes outside a study or clinical trial approved by the competent authority (External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: 2. It is prohibited to use any peptide product intended for research use on humans or for therapeutic purposes, except within a study or clinical trial approved by the competent authority, and in accordance with its protocol and the necessary regulatory approvals applicable in the State.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, importing any medical product, or the raw materials used to make it, requires an EDE approval or permit (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 31).
frameworks.quote: It is not permitted to import, export or re-export any Medical Product or any raw materials or pharmaceutical raw materials used in its manufacture except after obtaining approval or permit from the EDE.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the conditions for bringing a medicine in for personal use, carried by a traveller or sent by express courier, are set by executive regulation (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 35); the 2021 executive regulation sets them in its Annex 1 (Cabinet Resolution 90/2021, Art. 4).
frameworks.quote: The Executive Regulations of this Decree-Law shall specify the conditions, rules and controls for bringing, possessing or obtaining a Medical Product with any person upon entering or leaving the State for personal use, or bringing or sending the Medical Product through express shipping institutions.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the EDE lets travellers bring medicines that are not narcotic or psychotropic without prior submission; narcotic and psychotropic (controlled) medicines may be carried within three months' need with a prescription or medical report, and residents can obtain EDE approval to import such medicines for personal use through shipping companies (EDE personal-import service, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: The service allows residents of the country to obtain approvals to import personal narcotic and psychotropic drugs through shipping companies. … it is allowed for those coming to the country to take narcotic medicine and psychotropics (controlled medications) with them within the limits of a quantity that does not exceed the patient's need for a maximum period of three months … If the medicine isn’t considered as Narcotics or Psychotropics, they can carry their medicines safely without any prior submission.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, facilities may not buy, accept or use peptide products from websites, social media, individual accounts or unlicensed or unverifiable suppliers, and products without full identification data (active substance, concentration, batch, expiry) may not be used (DHA External Circular 0867, 29 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: It is prohibited to purchase, accept, or use peptide products from websites, social media platforms, individual accounts, or unlicensed or unverifiable suppliers. Products lacking identification data, or with incomplete or ambiguous identification data, or that do not indicate the active substance, concentration, dose, batch, or expiration date, are considered high-risk products that may not be used in the facility.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, prescription-only medicines may not be sold or dispensed through websites or delivery apps unless a valid prescription from a licensed practitioner has been verified, and online delivery needs prior DoH approval (Circular 152/2026, 5 Aug 2026).
frameworks.quote: DoH emphasizes that Prescription Only Medicines (POM) shall not be sold or dispensed through websites or medication delivery applications, unless a valid medical prescription has been verified. The prescription must be issued by a licensed healthcare practitioner and must comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. … Obtain prior approval from the DoH before providing medication delivery services through the pharmaceutical facility’s website or medication delivery applications

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 brings cosmetics with a medical effect on the skin, hair or nails within its definition of medical products regulated by the EDE.
frameworks.quote: Cosmetics: Products with a medical effect that are used on the human body to produce a desired local effect on the skin, hair or nails and do not require a prescription or direct medical supervision for their sale when used.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the EDE registers 'healthcare products' not intended to diagnose, treat or prevent disease, including dietary supplements, herbal products and cosmetics with a medical effect, through a marketing authorisation valid for five years (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: This service enables applicants to register healthcare products, including general pharmaceutical products, which are used for the promotion of general human health and are not intended for the diagnosis, treatment, cure, or prevention of any disease. Such products do not require a prescription or direct medical supervision for their use. The scope includes dietary supplements, antiseptics and disinfectants, herbal products, and cosmetics with a medical effect. … Issue the marketing authorization certificate for healthcare products, valid for five years from the date of the committee’s approval.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, whether a borderline product (for example a peptide serum) needs an EDE marketing authorisation, and in which category, is settled by an EDE classification letter based on the product's presentation, composition, use and design (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: This service allows the classification of products of all types and forms based on Presentation /Composition / Use and Design. … The classification letter determines the regulatory category of the product in terms of the requirement for  marketing authorization with the Emirates Drug Establishment.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, ordinary cosmetics and personal-care products are a MoIAT-regulated product category under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014 (the UAE control system for cosmetics and personal care products), needing a conformity certificate backed by accredited test reports, a formula declaration and a product safety report.
frameworks.quote: Test Report from accredited and recognized laboratory according to Gulf standard, UAE.S GSO 1943 … Formula Declaration with ingredients and percentage issued by the manufacturer. … Cosmetics and personal care … قرار مجلس الوزراء رقم (18) لسنة 2014 … النظام الإماراتي للرقابة على مستحضرات التجميل والعناية الشخصية … Product safety report according to Annex No. 3 of the cabinet resolution No. 18 of 2014
frameworks.quoteEn: Test Report from accredited and recognized laboratory according to Gulf standard, UAE.S GSO 1943 … Formula Declaration with ingredients and percentage issued by the manufacturer. … Cosmetics and personal care … Cabinet Resolution No. (18) of 2014 … UAE system for the control of cosmetics and personal care products … Product safety report according to Annex No. 3 of the cabinet resolution No. 18 of 2014

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, some topical peptide products with a hair or skin claim are registered by the EDE as general-sale-list (GSL) health products rather than medicines, e.g. Martiderm Anti Hair-Loss Ampoules containing biotinoyl tripeptide-1 (registered 24 Aug 2022, pharmacy-only) (EDE register, 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: MARTIDERM ANTI HAIR-LOSS AMPOULES … Classification GSL Products Dispensing mode Pharmacy Only (P) Country of origin Spain Registration date 2022-08-24 … Biotinoyl Tripeptide-1 0.000600

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, Dubai Municipality evaluates, registers, releases and monitors cosmetic products on the market, with registration through its Montaji+ platform (DM, 27 Oct 2025).
frameworks.quote: Through its presence, the Municipality is highlighting its comprehensive role in overseeing the evaluation, registration, release, and post-market monitoring of cosmetic products in the emirate. Central to its exhibition is Montaji+ , the Municipality’s upgraded digital platform that integrates artificial intelligence to streamline product registration

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH classes topical cosmetic peptides with no systemic effect as low-risk products that stay under existing regulatory pathways, while systemic, regenerative or weakly evidenced peptides face enhanced controls (Circular 148/2026, 31 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: 1. Low-risk peptides Products: These include products that have no systematic effect (e.g., topical cosmetic peptides) which will remain subject to existing regulatory pathways. 2. Moderate- and high-risk peptides: including products that have systemic effects (clinical), regenerative applications, or products supported only by emerging or insufficient clinical evidence, are subject to enhanced regulatory controls, strengthened quality assurance requirements, and stricter clinical governance, consistent with the above standard.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, food supplements are medical products under Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, defined as oral products that support the diet and do not treat, diagnose or prevent disease.
frameworks.quote: Food Supplements: Products taken orally that support the human diet and do not treat, diagnose, or prevent diseases. They consist of natural or partially manufactured products, or both, and do not require a prescription or direct medical supervision when used.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, a company registering a healthcare product such as a supplement with the EDE must declare it free of hormones, steroids, antibiotics, heavy metals and pig derivatives (EDE healthcare-product requirements, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: A statement issued by the company confirming that the product to be registered is free of hormones, heavy metals, antibiotics, steroids, pig derivatives and any other natural or chemical substances that have a harmful impact on human beings biologically and behaviorally

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, the DoH keeps a list of adulterated or contaminated supplements claimed for bodybuilding, sexual enhancement, weight reduction or cosmetic uses (DoH awareness page, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: The Department of Health - Abu Dhabi list of adulterated products include any adulterated or contaminated supplement that is claimed to be used as bodybuilding, sexual enhancement, weight reduction, cosmetic or any other miscellaneous health related reasons.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, advertising or promoting any medical product by any means, including social media, requires EDE approval, and advertising controlled or semi-controlled products to the public is prohibited (Federal Decree-Law 38/2024, Art. 44).
frameworks.quote: 1. It is prohibited to advertise, publicize or promote Medical Products by any means, whether visual, written, audible or on social media, unless approved by the EDE. 2. Advertising, publicity or promotion to the public of controlled, semi-controlled, hazardous or toxic chemical precursors, products or substances, whether for human or veterinary use, is prohibited.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, an EDE licence to advertise a medical product requires a valid EDE marketing authorisation for the product (only products exempted by the Cabinet under Art. 5(3) of Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 are excused), a licensed pharmaceutical or healthcare establishment as applicant, and truthful, evidence-based content matching the approved indications (EDE service page, read 25 Sep 2026).
frameworks.quote: A valid Marketing Authorisation from EDE must exist for the medical product to be advertised. Products exempted from the Marketing Authorisation requirement under the provisions of Clause (3) of Article (5) of Federal Decree-Law No. (38) are excluded from this condition … The applicant must be a licensed pharmaceutical establishment or a licensed healthcare establishment … The advertising material must be truthful, non-misleading, and supported by evidence reflecting the approved information and approved indications of the medical product

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, the federal health-advertisement regulation (Cabinet Resolution 7/2007) bars anyone from advertising or promoting products presented as related to a medical product without prior authorisation, and bans terms such as 'the only', 'unique' and 'best product'.
frameworks.quote: No natural or legal person may advertise or promote the sale of products related to or that are likely to make anyone believe that such an advertisement or promotion is related to any medical product without prior authorization from the Ministry of Health. … Using words like 'the only', 'unique', 'best product', 'Beware of imitation!', 'Don't miss!' must be avoided.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, the DHA bans misleading or unproven peptide claims, including anti-aging, cell regeneration, weight loss, muscle building and improved appearance, unless the use is within the product's approved status, and requires any promotion of unregistered materials, including through influencers or social media, to stop (29 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: It is prohibited to make misleading or scientifically unproven claims, including claims related to anti-aging or cell regeneration, or improving immunity, energy, or focus, or weight loss, muscle building, improving athletic performance, treating hormonal or sexual disorders, or improving appearance or public health in a guaranteed or risk-free manner, or any other therapeutic or physiological use, unless such use is approved and permitted within the regulatory status of the product. 2. Any advertising, promotion, or direct or indirect marketing of unregistered or unlicensed materials must be stopped, whether through the health facility, doctors, websites, social media platforms, phone messages, promotional offers, influencers, or any other media outlet.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, DHA-licensed professionals may not advertise on social media under titles that differ from their DHA licence, such as 'Aesthetic Specialist or Consultant', 'Cosmetologist' or 'Anti-Aging Specialist or Consultant' (DHA social-media advertising standard v1.1, effective 3 Oct 2022).
frameworks.quote: DHA licensed health facilities’ staff and all healthcare professionals shall refrain from using any other names or specialty titles that is different from their DHA license; such as Cosmetic Specialist or Consultant, Aesthetic Specialist or Consultant, Aesthetician, Cosmetologist, Diet Specialist or Consultant, Beauty Specialist or Consultant, Anti-Aging Specialist or Consultant, Cosmetic or Beauty Expert, .etc.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, social-media content from professionals, influencers or staff that names a health facility must be approved by its medical director, and absolute claims such as 'safest', 'magic', 'miraculous', '100%', 'has no side effects' or 'immediate results' must not be used (DHA social-media advertising standard v1.1).
frameworks.quote: Healthcare professionals, influencers and/or health facility administrative staff promoting any activity, healthcare service or outcomes specifying the health facility name and/or location should ensure the Medical Director (MD) of the health facility approves the SMA content. … Absolute statements, exaggerated claims and alarming expressions such as, but not limited to; unique, one of a kind, the best, exclusive, safest, the only, incomparable, unprecedented, best product, magic, miraculous, assured success, very limited quantity, has no side effects, get money back, 100%, absolutely certain, distinguished, famous, pioneer and immediate results must not be used.

frameworks.statement: In Dubai, the DHA recirculated its social-media advertising standard to all licensed private facilities and professionals on 17 Aug 2026, warning that non-compliance will lead to disciplinary action.
frameworks.quote: All health facilities and professionals are expected to adhere to the terms and conditions mentioned in the new Standards. Failure for compliance with this will result in taking the suitable disciplinary actions in regards.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, healthcare providers may not promote peptide therapies with misleading or unsubstantiated claims, or advertise, market or publish media content about them without prior approval from the DoH and relevant authorities (Circular 148/2026, 31 July 2026).
frameworks.quote: 5. Healthcare providers shall not promote peptide therapies through misleading or unsubstantiated therapeutic claims; 6. Healthcare providers and facilities shall not advertise, market, or publish media content relating to peptide therapies without obtaining prior approval from the DoH and relevant authorities;

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, emerging and non-monographed compounded substances such as peptides may not be advertised, promoted or marketed, directly or indirectly, to patients or healthcare professionals (DoH compounding standard, August 2026).
frameworks.quote: Emerging and non-monographed substances shall not be advertised, promoted, or marketed directly or indirectly to patients or healthcare professionals.

frameworks.statement: In Abu Dhabi, health advertisements, including press releases, are submitted for DoH approval through the health-advertisement registration service on the TAMM platform under DoH Chairman Resolution 37/2019 (Health Media & Advertising Regulations) (Circular 69/2026, 29 Apr 2026).
frameworks.quote: In reference to the Chairman of Department of Health Resolution No. (37) of 2019 regarding Health Media & Advertising Regulations … Please note that these need to be submitted through the Health Advertisement Registration Service on the “TAMM” platform, which will help expedite the approval procedures while ensuring that media content complies with the applicable regulatory standards.

frameworks.statement: In the UAE, injectable and oral testosterone, parenteral nandrolone, stanozolol, mesterolone and somatropin are semi-controlled drugs (SCD) under MOHAP Ministerial Decision 306/2023 (signed 24 Oct 2023), while topical forms of listed actives stay Prescription Only unless stated otherwise.
frameworks.quote: Oral dosage form & parenteral of these active ingredients will be considered as SCD. Topical preparations of these active ingredients will remain as POM unless otherwise stated. … 61. Mesterolone … 69. Nandrolone (parenteral form) … 93. Somatropin 94. Stanozolol … 96. Testosterone (oral & parenteral forms only)
frameworks.quoteEn: Oral dosage form & parenteral of these active ingredients will be considered as SCD. authorFindings: Regulator: medicine registration, import permits, advertising licences for medical products, the controlled and semi-controlled lists and compounding-pharmacy GCP certificates now sit with the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE), created by Federal Decree-Law 28/2023 (in force 30 Sep 2023) to succeed MOHAP. Official translations name it differently ('UAE Drug Corporation' on the legislation portal, 'Emirates Pharmaceutical Corporation' in DHA's list, 'Emirates Medicines Corporation' on the EDE legislation page); use 'Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE)'. MOHAP letterhead appears on the circulars read up to October 2024 (the Mounjaro alert says 'registered in MOHAP'); 2025-2026 circulars and approvals come from the EDE, although DHA attributed the June 2025 Melanotan II circular to MOHAP while DoH attributed the same warning to the EDE.

Off-label prescribing is conditioned in statute: Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 Art. 42(1) allows uses outside the leaflet, or a product never submitted for marketing approval, only when necessary, with no equivalent alternative and with the patient's approval (ae-fdl-38-2024).

Dubai and Abu Dhabi diverged on peptides within two days: DHA (29 Jul 2026) prohibits any peptide product not registered or licensed with the EDE and any research-use peptide outside approved trials; DoH (31 Jul 2026) runs a risk-tiered model with compounding through licensed pharmacies, EDE-overseen APIs, full traceability, consent covering regulatory status and prior approval of any advertising, and its August 2026 compounding standard treats peptides as emerging substances usable only if monographed, an approved-medicine component or on the DoH registry. Notes must name the emirate (ae-dha-cir-peptides-2026, ae-doh-cir-148-2026, ae-doh-compounding-std-2026).

Federal compounding: products compounded in licensed compounding pharmacies need no marketing approval (Art. 5(2)), but compounded essential copies of EDE-approved products are barred unless no commercial product can deliver the benefit (Art. 95(4)); since semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy injection and tablets, Rybelsus) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro) are registered, this copy rule bears directly on compounded GLP-1s. This is an inference from the two articles: no EDE statement on compounded GLP-1s was found.

Growth hormone and anabolic steroids are 'semi-controlled' medicines, not scheduled narcotics: every registered somatropin brand is dispensed as SCD, as are injectable testosterone, nandrolone, stanozolol and mesterolone; oral tretinoin, isotretinoin and acitretin are SCD too. Public advertising of controlled and semi-controlled products is banned (ae-mohap-md-306-2023, ae-ede-register, ae-fdl-38-2024).
Hair-loss products: no oral minoxidil product is registered (all 17 minoxidil entries are topical), while a topical finasteride spray (Fincrezo 2.275 mg/ml) has been registered since March 2025.

Recent EDE approvals relevant to the course: oral Wegovy (announced 1 June 2026, second country worldwide), orforglipron as Foundayo (3 April 2026, second country worldwide, months after the EDE's December 2025 warning about falsified 'orforglipron'), and upadacitinib (Rinvoq) for non-segmental vitiligo (17 Aug 2026, first country worldwide) (ae-ede-news-oral-wegovy, ae-ede-news-orforglipron, ae-ede-news-rinvoq-vitiligo). Ritlecitinib (Litfulo 50 mg) is also in the register.

Skin-clinic enforcement: exosome and PDRN products, including 'skin boosters' used with microneedling or mesotherapy, are unauthorised (EDE Circular 40/2026, 11 Sep 2026); glutathione injections for skin whitening are unregistered and must not be used (MOHAP, Oct 2021); Melanotan II warnings from MOHAP/EDE (June 2025) and DoH (July 2025); counterfeit and stolen Ozempic/Mounjaro alerts from 2024 to 2026.

Selling from clinics: licensed professionals other than pharmacists may not sell any medical product, directly or indirectly, without Ministry or health-authority approval (Art. 42(5)); only pharmaceutical establishments may sell prescription-only medicines (Art. 40); in Abu Dhabi, prescription-only medicines may be sold online only against a verified prescription (Circular 152/2026).

Cosmetics run on three tracks: ordinary cosmetics (MoIAT conformity under Cabinet Resolution 18/2014, plus Dubai Municipality Montaji registration in Dubai), 'cosmetics with a medical effect' registered by the EDE as healthcare products, and medicines. The EDE classification letter settles borderline products; Abu Dhabi treats topical cosmetic peptides as low risk.

Advertising: every medical-product advertisement, social media included, needs an EDE licence tied to a valid marketing authorisation and the approved indications, so unregistered peptides cannot lawfully be advertised. Dubai also bans titles such as 'Anti-Aging Specialist' or 'Aesthetic Consultant' and absolute claims.

Publication caution: the DoH circulars read (10/2025, 112/2025, 48/2026, 69/2026, 148/2026, 152/2026) say they 'should not be used as content for media publication', and the EDE and MOHAP circulars (EDE 20/2025, 31/2026, 40/2026; MOHAP 9217/2024) say they 'should not be used for media publication'. The integrator may prefer to keep those quotes in this file only (the registry's --no-quote-hosts option works per host: www.doh.gov.ae; the EDE/MOHAP circulars are hosted on www.dha.gov.ae, which also hosts DHA standards without that restriction).

Advertising compounded products: the EDE advertising licence requires a valid marketing authorisation and excuses only products exempted by the Cabinet under Art. 5(3); compounded products are exempt from marketing approval under Art. 5(2) instead, so on the service page's wording they cannot obtain an advertising licence (an inference; no EDE statement on advertising compounded products was found).
